text:
Yahoo Sports said it this week: Ville Koivunen's play is beginning to impress. The 23-year-old Finn has 7 points in 15 games for Pittsburgh, matching his total from 39 games last season, and he's playing a bit more lately.

Among forwards picked 41st to 61st since 2005 with four-plus seasons, the median first full season was 0.30 points a game, and only 64 of 188 reached 200 NHL games. Koivunen is at 0.47. That's a meaningful start for a second-round pick Carolina took in 2021 and Pittsburgh brought over.

The underlying numbers back it modestly. The Penguins take 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five. Evolving-Hockey's small sample from last season had him in the 92nd percentile at taking chances away, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (nine games) credits him with clean exits, 63% with possession. He shoots rarely and lacks speed (19th percentile in bursts), so he wins with his head. He played just 8:54 against Boston, then bounced back. We project about 31 points.
headline: Koivunen is beginning to impress
